mainTopic: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר on renting to a כותי, רבא's ruling on Jew-גוי partnerships split by days or years, and the opening משנה of the second chapter
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids renting a field to a כותי but allows renting to a גוי. He does not accept the idea of אריסותא, that a sharecropper works only for himself. A גוי obeys when told not to work on forbidden days, but a כותי will not obey because he thinks he knows better. The גמרא adds that he meant two reasons: לפני עור, and that the field is called by the owner's name. Next, רבא permits saffron growers to split their field, with the גוי taking שבת and the Jew taking Sunday. רבינא challenges him from a ברייתא, and רבא is embarrassed until it turns out the partners had agreed at the start. רב גביהה tells the story differently: the case was about ערלה years, רבינא supported רבא, and there was no embarrassment. The גמרא then asks about partners who said nothing at the start and finds that the ברייתא cannot settle it. The chapter ends, and a new משנה forbids leaving an animal in a גוי's inn and being alone with גוים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not accept the sharecropper rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not hold that a sharecropper works only for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not accept the idea that a sharecropper works for his own share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the reason 'the sharecropper works for himself' does not save the case of the כותי. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר simply does not accept that reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, a field rented to a sharecropper could be allowed because he is working for his own share, not for the Jewish owner. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rejects that idea. In his view, the sharecropper's work still counts as connected to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharecropping; the idea that a sharecropper works for his own share
He does not hold of it / does not accept it

phrases.english: Sharecropping, to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a sharecropper works for his own share and not for the owner.

phrases.english: he does not hold of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲרִיסוּתָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from just before this section about why the sharecropper rule does not permit renting to a כותי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise: this תנא does not accept the principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Renting to a כותי should be allowed because a sharecropper works for himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rejects that principle, so it cannot permit the case.

steps.title: Then why is a gentile allowed?
steps.stepSummary: If the sharecropper rule is rejected, the גמרא asks why renting to a גוי is still allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, a gentile: what is the reason it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not use the sharecropper rule, why is a גוי allowed to rent the field?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking away the sharecropper rule seems to take away the reason a גוי was allowed too. The גמרא now needs a new reason to explain the difference between a גוי and a כותי.

phrases.english: But a gentile, what is the reason it is permitted?
phrases.notes: He means: why may a Jew rent his field to a gentile?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 1: without the sharecropper rule, the permission for a גוי needs a new explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason renting a field to a גוי is permitted according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: A gentile obeys when told not to work
steps.stepSummary: A גוי is allowed because we can tell him not to work on those days, and he listens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we tell him not to work on those days, and he obeys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: a גוי can be told not to work on the forbidden days, and he will listen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission for a גוי does not depend on the sharecropper rule. It depends on a practical fact: the owner can set a condition, and the גוי keeps it. So no forbidden work will be done on the owner's field.

keyTerms.meaning: We say to him / we tell him

phrases.english: Because we tell him, and he obeys.
phrases.notes: We tell him not to work on the days work is forbidden for us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גוי can be told not to work on those days, and he complies.

steps.title: Tell the Samaritan the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: we could also tell a כותי not to work, and he would obey.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Samaritan too: we can tell him, and he will obey!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If telling him works for a גוי, it should work for a כותי as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason seems to apply to a כותי just as well as to a גוי. If so, there is still no explanation for why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids renting to a כותי.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan; keeps some מצוות but does not follow חז"ל

phrases.english: A Samaritan too, we can tell him and he will obey!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason in step 3, that we can tell him and he obeys
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason should apply to a כותי, so it does not explain why only the כותי is forbidden.

steps.title: A Samaritan will not listen
steps.stepSummary: A כותי does not obey, because he thinks he knows the הלכה better than the Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Samaritan does not obey, because he says: I know more than you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A כותי will not follow the Jew's instructions, because he trusts his own knowledge more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי has no opinion of his own about these laws, so he simply does what he is told. A כותי has his own way of keeping מצוות and will argue that working on those days is allowed. So the condition cannot be trusted with him.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a גוי is allowed because he obeys the owner's instructions. A כותי is forbidden because he will not obey, since he thinks he knows better.

phrases.english: A Samaritan does not obey,
because he says: I am more learned than you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases by how each person behaves
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כותי will obey instructions just like a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כותי will not obey, because he relies on his own knowledge.

steps.title: Why not use the reason of לפני עור?
steps.stepSummary: If the כותי himself will do forbidden work, why give the reason 'called by his name' instead of לפני עור?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why specifically 'because it is called by his name'? Let him get it from 'Do not put a stumbling block before the blind'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר chose the reason 'the field is called by the owner's name.' A simpler reason seems to be available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just said the כותי will work on days that are forbidden even for him. Renting him the field would then help him sin, which falls under the איסור of לפני עור. So why did רבי שמעון בן אלעזר need the weaker-sounding reason about the field carrying the owner's name?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it instead from…
Do not put a stumbling block before the blind; do not help someone sin
It is called by his name; people link the field to its owner

phrases.english: If so, why specifically
"because it is called by his name"?
phrases.notes: This is the reason רבי שמעון בן אלעזר himself gave: people call the field by the Jewish owner's name.

phrases.english: Let him derive it because of
"Do not put a stumbling block before the blind"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 5: if the כותי will not obey, a different reason seems more obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gave: 'because it is called by his name'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the כותי will sin, לפני עור is a simpler and stronger reason, so why not use it?

steps.title: He gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר meant both reasons: לפני עור, and also that the field is called by the owner's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is saying one reason and another: one, because of 'before the blind,' and another, because it is called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר meant two reasons. לפני עור is the first, and 'called by his name' is an extra one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason he spelled out does not replace לפני עור. He is adding a second reason on top of it. This closes the discussion about the כותי.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying one reason and also another

steps.whatToRemember: Renting a field to a כותי is forbidden for two reasons: לפני עור, and because the field is called by the Jewish owner's name.

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and another:
one, because of "before the blind";
and another, because it is called by his name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stated reason is the only reason, which is strange when לפני עור is available.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both reasons are meant: לפני עור, plus 'called by his name.'

steps.title: רבא permits the saffron growers' arrangement
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: a גוי worked a shared saffron field on שבת and the Jew on Sunday, and רבא permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were saffron growers: the gentile took the field on שבת and the Jew on Sunday. They came before רבא, and he permitted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a story about a ruling. רבא allowed a Jew and a גוי to share a field by splitting the days, with the גוי taking שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that the גוי's work on שבת might count as work done for the Jewish partner. רבא ruled the arrangement is allowed. This ruling sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunday, the first day of the week

phrases.english: There were certain saffron growers
where the gentile took the field on שבת,
and the Jew on Sunday.
They came before רבא,
and he permitted them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about Jew-גוי partnerships and שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא permits a partnership in which the גוי takes the field on שבת and the Jew on Sunday.

steps.title: רבינא objects from a ברייתא about partners
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבא with a ברייתא: a Jew may not tell his גוי partner 'take שבת and I'll take a weekday' unless they agreed at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected to רבא: A Jew and a gentile who took a field in partnership: the Jew may not say to the gentile, 'Take your share on שבת and I will take mine on a weekday.' But if they stipulated at the start, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא begins a challenge to רבא's ruling by quoting a ברייתא. The quote continues past this point, so the גמרא is setting up the full challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids a Jew to tell his גוי partner to take שבת while he takes a weekday, because then the גוי's שבת work is partly for the Jew. It permits this only if they agreed at the very beginning. רבא permitted the saffron growers without asking about any agreement made at the start, so his ruling seems to clash with this ברייתא. The next step finishes the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a condition at the start

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not ban the day-split completely. It bans it only when there was no agreement at the start. That detail is what later saves רבא in step 11.

phrases.english: רבינא raised an objection to רבא:
A Jew and a gentile who took on a field in partnership,
the Jew may not say to the gentile:
"Take your share for שבת, and I will take mine for a weekday."
But if they made this condition at the start, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission for the saffron growers' arrangement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids the שבת and weekday split unless they agreed at the start. רבא permitted the saffron growers without any such condition.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא, and רבא is embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the partners did not stipulate and only later calculated the shares, it is forbidden. רבא is embarrassed by this challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they came to calculate afterward, it is forbidden. רבא was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבינא's ברייתא. The challenge hits רבא, and he is embarrassed because his ruling seems to go against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows the split only if they agreed at the start. If they just work and later count up days to even out the profit, the גוי's שבת work turns out to have been done for the Jew. So רבא's permission for the saffron partners looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They came to calculate, meaning they figured out the shares afterward

phrases.english: And if they came to calculate, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: This is still the ברייתא from the last step. Here they had no deal at the start and only counted the days afterward.

phrases.english: He was embarrassed.
phrases.notes: That is רבא, because the ברייתא seemed to go against his ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 9 and shows its effect on רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permission for the saffron partners in step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids the split when it was not stipulated at the start. רבא permitted it without asking about any stipulation.

steps.title: It turns out they had stipulated at the start
steps.stepSummary: In the end it came out that the saffron partners had made the arrangement at the start, so רבא's ruling was correct even according to the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end the matter came to light: they had made the stipulation from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The facts of the case come out, and they save רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא permits the split when there was a deal from the beginning. Since the saffron partners had made such a deal, their case fits the permitted side of the ברייתא. רבא was right after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter was revealed, it came to light

phrases.english: In the end the matter came to light
that they had stipulated from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אִיגַּלַּאי מִלְּתָא דְּהִתְנוּ מֵעִיקָּרָא הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 9-10 by clarifying the facts of the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the facts: the case fits the permitted side of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The saffron partners had no stipulation, so רבא's ruling goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: They did stipulate at the start, so רבא's permission matches the ברייתא.
steps.whatToRemember: A split where the גוי takes שבת and the Jew takes a weekday is allowed only if it was agreed at the start. Counting up afterward is forbidden.

steps.title: רב גביהה's version: the case was about ערלה saplings
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהה says the real story was about a partnership in ערלה saplings. The גוי took the ערלה years, the Jew took the permitted years, and רבא permitted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהה from בי כתיל said: there were ערלה saplings. The גוי would take the profit of the ערלה years, and the Jew the permitted years. They came before רבא, and he permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: A different version of the story is given. Now the case is about the years of ערלה, not about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same as before: the גוי takes the forbidden period and the Jew takes the permitted period. In this version רבא again permitted it. The גמרא will next check how this version fits with רבינא's challenge and רבא's embarrassment.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree's first three years, which a Jew may not eat or benefit from

phrases.english: רב גביהה from בי כתיל said:
There were certain saplings of ערלה,
the גוי would take the profit of the ערלה years,
and the Jew the permitted years.
They came before רבא, and he permitted it to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the story about רבא's ruling from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partnership where the גוי takes the ערלה years and the Jew takes the permitted years is allowed, according to רבא.

steps.title: But רבינא challenged רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב גביהה's version fits with the report that רבינא challenged רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבינא challenge רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב גביהה's version, since the earlier story said רבינא raised a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבינא brought a ברייתא against רבא, that does not seem to fit רב גביהה's version of events. The גמרא wants to know what happened to that challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a challenge against him

phrases.english: But didn't רבינא challenge רבא?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רב גביהה's version from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב גביהה's version of the story
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first version says רבינא brought a ברייתא against רבא. That needs to be explained in רב גביהה's version.

steps.title: רבינא was supporting רבא
steps.stepSummary: In רב גביהה's version, רבינא quoted the ברייתא to support רבא, not to challenge him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was supporting him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבינא's ברייתא was brought as support for רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a split is permitted when agreed at the start. In רב גביהה's version this fits רבא's ruling, so רבינא used it to back רבא up.

phrases.english: He was supporting him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting רבינא's role: support instead of challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבינא used the ברייתא to attack רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this version, רבינא used the ברייתא to support רבא.

steps.title: But רבא was embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבינא was supporting רבא, why was רבא embarrassed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't he embarrassed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again: the story said רבא was embarrassed, which only makes sense if he was challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Embarrassment points to an attack, not a support. So the גמרא asks how רב גביהה's version deals with that detail.

phrases.english: But he was embarrassed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבינא was supporting רבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it was only support, there is no reason for רבא to be embarrassed, yet the story says he was.

steps.title: The embarrassment never happened
steps.stepSummary: According to רב גביהה, רבא was never embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those things never happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in רב גביהה's version, the embarrassment simply did not happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב גביהה does not try to explain the embarrassment. He rejects that part of the story completely. So in his version רבא's ruling stood without any problem.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions. In the first, רבא was challenged and embarrassed, then saved because there was a stipulation. In רב גביהה's version, the case was about ערלה, רבינא supported רבא, and there was no embarrassment.

phrases.english: Those things never happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the event: the embarrassment is not part of this version.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was embarrassed, so רבינא must have challenged him.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רב גביהה's version, there was no embarrassment at all.

steps.title: What if they said nothing at the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the partners neither stipulated at the start nor calculated afterward, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: when it was left unspecified, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. The ברייתא covered a deal at the start (permitted) and calculating afterward (forbidden), but not the middle case of saying nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unclear case is partners who never spelled anything out. Is that treated like the permitted case or the forbidden one? The גמרא is setting up a search for an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with בָּאוּ לְחֶשְׁבּוֹן. There they calculated afterward. Here they simply never said anything either way.

phrases.english: They asked:
When it was left unspecified, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question based on the two cases in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for partners who neither stipulated at the start nor calculated afterward.

steps.title: Proof attempt: the ברייתא implies unspecified is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the ברייתא that only a stipulation at the start permits, so an unspecified case is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if they stipulated at the start, it is permitted. This implies that if it was unspecified, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question by reading the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives permission only when they stipulated at the start. That suggests anything less, including saying nothing, is forbidden. This is a reading of the wording, so the גמרא may still test it next.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies, introducing what we learn from the wording

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If they stipulated at the start, it is permitted,
which implies that if it was unspecified, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אִם הִתְנוּ מִתְּחִילָּה — מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That an unspecified partnership is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: What the ברייתא implies by allowing the split only when it was stipulated at the start

steps.title: The last clause of the ברייתא points the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The last clause of the ברייתא forbids only partners who 'came to calculate,' which suggests that an unspecified case is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now read the last clause: if they came to calculate, it is forbidden. That means if they made no arrangement at all, it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof from step 18. It reads the last clause of the same ברייתא, and that clause leads to the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, the first clause seemed to say that only a deal made at the start permits, so an unspecified case would be forbidden. The last clause names only the case of calculating afterward as forbidden. That suggests an unspecified case, with no deal and no calculation, is permitted. So the two clauses point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: They came to calculate, meaning they settled the accounts afterward
An unspecified case, where nothing was arranged

steps.confusionAlert: Both inferences come from the very same ברייתא. The גמרא is not bringing a new source. It is reading the other half of the same text.

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
If they came to calculate, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: He means partners who made no deal at the start and then tried to split up the שבת profits afterward.

phrases.english: so without any arrangement, it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It counters the inference from the first clause in step 18 with an opposite inference from the last clause.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that an unspecified partnership is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The last clause of the same ברייתא implies the opposite, so the inference from the first clause cannot be relied on.

steps.title: No conclusion can be drawn from this ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Since the two clauses lead to opposite results, the גמרא concludes that the ברייתא cannot answer the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, nothing can be learned from this ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the investigation. This ברייתא cannot decide the case of partners who made no deal and did not calculate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each clause can be read in a way that points to a different answer. Because of that, neither inference is reliable. The question from step 17 is left without proof from this source.

keyTerms.meaning: Nothing can be learned from it

steps.whatToRemember: When the first and last clauses of a source lead to opposite inferences, the גמרא often concludes that the source proves nothing either way.

phrases.english: Rather, from this
nothing can be learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It draws the result of the clash between steps 18 and 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא does not settle the law of an unspecified partnership, so the question remains open.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter לפני אידיהן
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line for the first chapter of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'Before their festivals.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the first chapter. It is a traditional closing formula, not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן expresses the learner's wish to come back and learn the chapter again. The chapter is named after its opening words, לפני אידיהן.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said when finishing a chapter
Before their festivals; the name of the first chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you,
chapter 'Before their festivals.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It closes the whole chapter after the final discussion in steps 17 to 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first chapter of עבודה זרה is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: not leaving an animal, a woman, or oneself alone with גוים
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens with three rules. Do not keep an animal in a גוי's inn, a woman should not be alone with גוים, and a person should not be alone with them, each because of a specific suspicion.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not keep an animal in the inns of גוים, because they are suspected of bestiality. A woman may not be alone with them, because they are suspected of forbidden relations. A person may not be alone with them, because they are suspected of bloodshed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It gives three parallel rules about situations a Jew must avoid with גוים, and each rule comes with its own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three rules follow the same pattern: a forbidden situation, then 'because they are suspected of' a particular sin. The first rule keeps a Jew from placing his animal where a sin may be done with it. The second protects a woman, and the third protects any person's life. The משנה is setting up the topics the גמרא will now discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not keep or station an animal

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the main source for the rules about leaving animals with, and being alone with, people suspected of these sins. The rest of the chapter builds on it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not keep an animal
in the inns of gentiles,
because they are suspected of bestiality,
and a woman may not be alone with them,
because they are suspected of forbidden relations,
and a person may not be alone with them,
because they are suspected of bloodshed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַעֲמִידִין בְּהֵמָה בְּפוּנְדְּקָאוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not keep an animal in a גוי's inn, and a woman or a man should not be alone with גוים, because of suspected bestiality, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.
